verdict: MRVL investor day confirms 18-socket custom silicon sweep and $94B TAM; NVDA ATH Oct 6 then modest pullback; HBM supply gap persists; DRAM cycle moderating; solar 232 tariffs effective Dec 4 reshape supply chain.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (Last 24–72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing:** Moderating but still positive. Q3 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices tracking +13–18% QoQ (TrendForce), a sharp step-down from Q2's ~+58–63% and Q1's record +90–95%. Q4 expected positive but slower still. HBM spot data remains thin and conflicting; HBM3E estimates range from $13–17/GB to ~20% YoY increase on annual agreements. No fresh Oct QoQ print found. Direction: **decelerating bull**.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk:** No Oct news on correction. All three suppliers ramping in H2: SK Hynix began HBM4 mass shipments Q2 and scaling 2H; Micron targeting ~100K wafers/mo by year-end (up from ~40K); Samsung targeting ~250K wafers/mo by end-2026. TrendForce still sees ~20% supply gap for full-year 2026. Baseline correction-risk signal (prices soften post-2026 as all three complete expansions) remains intact but no new confirmation this week. Direction: **supply tight through 2026, watch 2027**.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex:** Combined big-4 2026 capex guidance at $720–745B following latest earnings — above baseline $600–700B. Meta's H2 is back-loaded at $79–94B implied (vs. $50.9B H1 actual). No guide-down signal. Microsoft's apparent cut is an accounting reclassification, not real reduction. Direction: **bull**.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400/Helios & Custom ASICs:** No fresh Oct news. AMD Helios first shipments targeted end-Q3 2026; status update pending. Google Ironwood (TPU7x) GA since March 2026; AWS Trainium4 targeted late 2026/early 2027 with NVLink Fusion support. NVIDIA still ~80% AI accelerator spend. Direction: **neutral/watch**.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics:** No fresh Oct 9 news. NVIDIA's $4B commitment to Coherent + Lumentum (March 2026) remains baseline. Coherent FY2026 10-K confirmed ongoing global 6-inch InP expansion. CPO scale-out timeline unchanged; volume window remains 2027–2028. Direction: **neutral (InP constrained, long ramp)**.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** Section 232 signed Aug 6, 2026 — 15% tariff + minimum import price (MIP) floors ($0.22/W cells, $0.38/W modules) effective **December 4, 2026**. Module floor ~40% above current US median (~$0.27/W). FSLR (domestic thin-film, no Chinese polysilicon) is the structural winner. ENPH Q3 report Oct 27; FSLR ~Oct 29 — no Oct moves yet. Direction: **bull for FSLR, tariff headwind for Chinese-supply names**.

---

## Watchlist Movers (Oct 6–9)

| Name | Move | Catalyst |
|------|------|----------|
| **MRVL** | +~7% Oct 6, then −3.5% Oct 8 | Investor Day: 18 custom silicon sockets (5 XPU + 13 attach) across Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta + 2 emerging hyperscalers; $94B data center TAM by 2028 (vs prior $75B); $20B FY2028 revenue target; $70–90B FY2031 target; UBS Buy, PT raised to $350. Ex-div Oct 9 ($0.06). |
| **NVDA** | ATH hit Oct 6 ($243+), −0.74% Oct 7, premarket weak Oct 8 | All-time high mid-week; no single news catalyst; broad sector profit-taking on rising yields |
| **AVGO** | ~$364, premarket weak Oct 8 | Reportedly arranging $50B+ financing for custom AI chips with OpenAI (Bloomberg); FY2028 AI revenue 4x 2026 guidance intact |
| **AMD** | −1.8% premarket Oct 8 | Sector rotation; Citi PT raise (details unclear) |
| **HIVE** | No fresh Oct news | Last known: Aug $350M 5-yr GPU cloud contract; ARR target $200M by Q4 2026. Boden Sweden deal sign status unconfirmed. |
| **ENPH/FSLR** | No Oct moves | Reports Oct 27/~Oct 29; 232 tariff setup favors FSLR |
| **MU** | No fresh news | — |

*No notable moves on NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU, STX, RMBS, MRAM, SNDK/WDC, CIEN, COHR, LITE, NXT, ARRY this window.*

---

## Context vs Baseline

- DRAM moderation is on-script: Q1 spike was the peak; Q3/Q4 still positive but easy comps are gone.
- HBM sold-out 2026 narrative holds. 2027 correction risk thesis unchanged — no supplier has walked it back.
- MRVL's investor day is the clearest data point this week that custom ASIC share is accelerating: 18 sockets vs. prior estimates of 10–12 is a meaningful beat.
- AVGO–OpenAI financing story, if confirmed, would be another major custom-silicon validation.

---

## Signals Flashing

| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| DRAM pricing | Decelerating positive | Mild bull |
| HBM supply gap | Tight through 2026 | Bull (near-term) |
| Hyperscaler capex | Revised up, no guide-down | Bull |
| Custom ASIC share | Accelerating (MRVL 18 sockets) | Mixed (bull MRVL/AVGO; watch NVDA long-term) |
| Optical/InP | Constrained, slow CPO ramp | Neutral |
| Solar / 232 tariffs | FSLR structural winner post-Dec 4 | Bull FSLR |

---

## Most Important Development

**MRVL Investor Day (Oct 6):** Marvell revealed 18 custom silicon sockets — exceeding prior estimates — across all major US hyperscalers plus two emerging players, raised its 2028 data center TAM to $94B, and guided $20B FY2028 revenue. The stock's initial +7% pop and subsequent −3.5% giveback reflects profit-taking into strength (+156% past 6 months). This is the strongest single confirmation yet that custom ASIC share-shift is on schedule and accelerating; it is directly relevant to the NVIDIA long-term thesis and to AVGO's custom silicon pipeline.
